title: How did the first public libraries work?
sources: Library of Congress Franklin Subscription Library

lines.text: Today you can walk into a public library and borrow thousands of dollars in books completely free.
For centuries, books were rare luxury items owned exclusively by wealthy aristocrats and churches.
lines.caps: Books were rare *luxuries | owned only by the *super-rich

lines.text: In seventeen thirty-one, Benjamin Franklin and his friends pooled their money to launch America's first subscription lending library.
Members paid annual dues to share a communal collection of history, science, and philosophy books.
lines.caps: Members pooled money to *share | the cost of rare *books

lines.text: In the nineteenth century, cities introduced tax-supported free libraries open to all citizens regardless of wealth.
lines.caps: Cities voted for *free libraries | open to every *citizen!

lines.text: Steel magnate Andrew Carnegie personally funded over twenty-five hundred free public libraries across the globe.
lines.caps: Andrew Carnegie funded *2,500 free | libraries worldwide with steel *wealth

lines.text: Public libraries remain one of the purest sanctuaries of free knowledge in human history.
lines.caps: Sanctuaries of free *knowledge | open to anyone with *curiosity!
